conclusion: Not reached by static search. Among the 95 hash-verified cp312 wheels selected from the lock, crawl4ai 0.9.4 is the only distribution that imports nltk: 7 import statements in model_loader.py, chunking_strategy.py and legacy/llmtxt.py. Those sites use tokenization (sent_tokenize, word_tokenize, TextTilingTokenizer), corpora (stopwords, WordNetLemmatizer) and data management (nltk.data.find, nltk.download). None names an API listed by GHSA-8mgp-746c-j5xp, and the names TransitionParser, AveragedPerceptron, PerceptronTagger, save_to_json and save_maxent_params occur nowhere in the closure outside nltk, nor in the nltk modules behind the APIs crawl4ai uses. The recipe's own Python imports no nltk. The worker selects no nltk-using crawl4ai code: it passes apply_chunking=False to LLMExtractionStrategy (worker.py:156), whose run path has no nltk reference under either value, and it keeps CrawlerRunConfig's default RegexChunking. nltk 3.10.3 ships pathsec on (nltk/pathsec.py:28), so the advisory's enforcement precondition holds by default. No caller here lets input choose model import or export paths for the affected APIs. The lock still pins an OSV-affected nltk with no patched PyPI release, so this is a reachability finding, not a remediation.
limits: Static text search with ripgrep over unpacked wheels and recipe files: not a runtime trace, import-time observation or call-graph analysis.
Dynamic dispatch, getattr, and string-built or computed imports (for example importlib.import_module with a variable) may be missed; only literal patterns were searched.
Compiled extension modules were covered only by byte searches for nltk and the five API names; names built at runtime inside native code would not be found.

Scope is the 95 cp312 manylinux x86_64 wheels the lock selects for the recipe's Python 3.12 venv. The unclecode/crawl4ai container image that the recipe also runs (pins.json image digest) has its own Python environment and was not scanned.
Reachability inside nltk was checked by name search in nltk/tokenize/, nltk/corpus/, nltk/stem/wordnet.py, nltk/data.py and nltk/downloader.py, not with a full nltk call graph.
Advisory and release facts are as fetched on 2026-09-27, with the OSV and PyPI response hashes recorded; OSV records and PyPI releases can change later.
Nothing was installed, imported or executed, and no nltk data was downloaded; runtime behaviour such as the 'toknize' attribute access or nltk.download side effects was not observed.
The brief's Python 3.13 wheel set was not downloaded; binary wheels for other interpreters were not scanned.
